groups.title: Availability Architecture
groups.question: Explain how you would design an Azure workload to stay up when parts of the platform fail.

followUps.Availability Zones vs Availability Sets: What failure does an availability zone protect you from that an availability set does not?
followUps.RTO and RPO Design for Azure Workloads: How do RTO and RPO targets change the HA and DR design you would choose for a workload?

groups.title: Azure Traffic Manager and Front Door
groups.question: Explain how you would route users to the right region in a global application.

followUps.Traffic Manager Routing Methods: Why does DNS caching affect how fast Traffic Manager can fail over, and how does that touch your RTO?
followUps.Azure Front Door for Global HTTP Traffic: How does Front Door make a global HTTP app faster and safer than pointing users straight at a regional backend?

groups.title: Azure Site Recovery
groups.question: Walk through how you would recover workloads and data after a regional outage or a ransomware attack.

followUps.VM Replication and Failover: Why should you run test failovers with Site Recovery, and what can they reveal?
followUps.Azure Backup and Recovery Vaults: How do soft delete and immutable vaults protect backups, and why must you test restores?

groups.title: Chaos Engineering on Azure
groups.question: Explain how you would prove that a system is actually as reliable as its design claims.

followUps.Azure Chaos Studio: How would you plan a safe chaos experiment, and what kind of hidden weakness might it reveal?
followUps.Well-Architected Reliability Pillar: What does a reliability review against the Well-Architected Framework look for in a real workload?
